title: #include R headers after system headers
description: We are observing an LLVM change breaking compilation here because of a macro conflict in `<vector>` vs. `<Rinternals.h>`'s `length()`. FWIW this is in line with the recommended order in the Google C++ guide: https://google.github.io/styleguide/cppguide.html#Names_and_Order_of_Includes.

title: Sort files with C locale
description:
I think `decor::cpp_files()` should return a file listing according to an explicit fixed locale and C is the obvious choice. In particular, this eliminates nuisance churn in `R/cpp11.R` and `src/cpp11.cpp`, which are created by `cpp11::cpp_register()`. Below I describe how to reproduce the churn. The culprit in my current usage is the RStudio IDE.

There are a few ways to get the C locale ordering:

* Use `withr::with_locale()`. But withr isn't already a direct or indirect dependency, so I didn't do this.
* Inline an equivalent helper, like this one from roxygen2:
https://cs.github.com/r-lib/roxygen2/blob/39d2dbefddac508dba6bffdec3a625cac7af16bc/R/util-locale.R#L7
* Rely on vctrs, which is already in `Imports`. This is what I actually did. At this moment, C locale ordering is only exposed in `vctrs::vec_rank()`, so I used that and set vctrs minimum version accordingly. In the future, we can switch to `vec_sort_radix()`.

---

If you check out readr from current HEAD (a257bfb at the time I write this), the files `R/cpp11.R` and `src/cpp11.cpp` are generated from a listing of the C++ files sorted according to `en_US.UTF-8`.

With CRAN decor and RStudio Version 2022.12.0+353 (2022.12.0+353):

* If you do `devtools::clean_dll()` and `cpp11::cpp_register()`, in the Console, `R/cpp11.R` and `src/cpp11.cpp` do not change. Still picking up the ambient locale.
* If you do `devtools::clean_dll()` and `devtools::document()`, in the Console, `R/cpp11.R` and `src/cpp11.cpp` do not change. Still picking up the ambient locale.
* If you then do `devtools::clean_dll()` and **use RStudio** to do `devtools::document()` (from *Build* pane or keyboard shortcut), `R/cpp11.R` and `src/cpp11.cpp` will change. It appears that RStudio silently changes to the C locale during the execution of `document()`.
  - I don't see the same locale-switching behaviour if I use the IDE to `test()` or `check()`. Only `document()`.

After this PR, anyone using cpp11 might see one instance of churn, getting their `R/cpp11.R` and `src/cpp11.cpp` to be based on C-locale-ordering of source files, but then they should only change for legit reasons after that.

---

Added later: this is where the IDE is doing this. Probably not ideal behaviour in the current era, but possibly also not worth changing.

https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/blob/86ae4e281b82ad87ddce3247aab01144efdb6ecb/src/cpp/session/modules/build/SessionBuild.cpp#L544-L552

title: Changes for decor CRAN release
description:
These are all the changes I have made to adapt decor for use in cpp11, as well as get it ready for a CRAN release.

It now can find decorations with both comments or C++11 attributes.
I added some simple tests for all the existing functions. It has 100% coverage now, but I could probably write a few more for testing multiple decorations in multiple files.
I reduced the dependencies so it now only directly depends on `tibble`, `utils` and `vctrs`.
I added a readme, made RStudio the copyright holder and myself as the maintainer, if you would prefer to be the maintainer let me know.
Some additional things to prepare for a CRAN submission.

I verified that the code still seems to work for the arrow case, let me know if you discover this is not the case.

If these changes are acceptable to you it would be great if they could be merged and the repository moved to r-lib/decor.

If you would prefer not to incorporate these changes to this repo I can rename the package to something else and put it in r-lib (you would remain as an author of course).

Let me know, ideally I would like to submit decor to CRAN sometime next week.

title: Remove devtools dependency
description: This was causing about 40+ extra packages to be installed along with decor on arrow's CI. `devtools` was only used for `as.package`, which for `decor` basically just gives you some better error messages if you provide a bad path. Doesn't seem worth it IMO.
